topics.what_the_statute_regulates: The BGB regulates how the deposit must be held (separate from the landlord's own assets, § 551) and the landlord's pledge right over the tenant's movable property (§ 562, § 562a-d).
topics.what_is_governed_elsewhere: Deadlines for returning the deposit at the end of the tenancy are set by court decisions (case law of the BGH), not by the BGB. Typical court guidance is a few months after handover, but the statute itself is silent.

topics.what_the_statute_regulates: The BGB defines the rent-increase mechanics (§§ 558-559f) and references the ortsübliche Vergleichsmiete (usual local comparative rent).
topics.what_is_governed_elsewhere: The Mietspiegel (rent index) itself is a municipal instrument; how a city builds and updates its Mietspiegel is governed by the Mietspiegelverordnung (a federal ordinance) and municipal practice, not by the BGB text.

topics.what_the_statute_regulates: The BGB regulates that operating costs can be passed on and that annual settlement is due within 12 months (§ 556).
topics.what_is_governed_elsewhere: Which cost types count as Betriebskosten, and their caps, are set by the Betriebskostenverordnung (BetrKV), a separate ordinance not contained in the BGB.

topics.what_the_statute_regulates: The BGB contains the Mietpreisbremse mechanics (§§ 556d-556g): in designated areas the initial rent may not exceed the local comparative rent by more than 10 percent.
topics.what_is_governed_elsewhere: Which areas are designated (angespannte Wohnungsmärkte) is decided by state ordinances under § 556d Absatz 2 - the designations themselves are not in the BGB.
